projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 20+ device count paired with zero camera motion for four hours strongly suggests either a concentrated gathering in a camera-blind zone (like a basement or garage) or a network/IoT device count anomaly rather than normal household movement. This warrants a quick verification to ensure the kids' gathering is safe and supervised, or to rule out a smart home network glitch.

The persistent 20–23 device count with zero camera motion suggests either Miller’s friends are over in a single room with lights off, or a network glitch is inflating presence data. Steve should quickly verify occupancy or check the router to rule out phantom connections.

The sustained 20-22 device count paired with zero camera motion on a weekday evening strongly indicates a network presence detection anomaly (likely Wi-Fi scanning artifacts or gateway glitch) rather than actual occupancy, which could cause incorrect automations or mask real absence events.

The sustained 20-22 device count paired with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon strongly suggests unmonitored guests or a network registration anomaly, warranting a quick verification to ensure no unauthorized access or to confirm expected visitors.

The sustained 15–20 device count paired with zero camera motion over a four-hour weekday afternoon strongly indicates stationary connected devices (likely parked cars with Wi-Fi or phones left in a camera-blind zone) rather than active occupants, suggesting a low-activity gathering or parked vehicles rather than an empty house or security concern.

The device count spike to 20 around 15:50, followed by a drop to 18 with zero camera motion, indicates a temporary after-school gathering or device influx that has since settled; this cross-signal pattern confirms the home is in a low-activity state despite the high device count.

The persistent 15-18 device count paired with zero camera activity on a weekday afternoon strongly suggests the presence system is overcounting stationary IoT devices, or the cameras are offline. This warrants a quick diagnostic to ensure accurate occupancy tracking and security monitoring.

The consistent 16-18 device count paired with zero camera activity on a weekday afternoon indicates the home is unoccupied, with connected devices being stationary (routers, charging hubs, etc.) rather than active household members. This confirms a typical school/work schedule and helps prevent false presence alerts.

The stable presence of 16-18 mobile devices combined with zero camera activity on a weekday mid-morning strongly indicates the camera system may be offline or malfunctioning, as active children and dogs would typically trigger motion alerts. Verify camera connectivity to ensure security monitoring remains active.

The device count stabilizing at 16-18 after the 08:42 drop indicates most household members are likely still home, but the complete lack of camera activity for four hours suggests the cameras are offline, in privacy mode, or motion detection is disabled, leaving the home unmonitored during a typical active morning.
